utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a small problem with the probative piece of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This is document 4667, proposed by the other side. It has 144 pages, and the witness read a part of the page marked reference number 01520527, so we have this problem with such a voluminous document. The witness referred to just one page of this document and recognised it and we feel that as such, in this form, it cannot be admitted into the file. We already had cases before of just the individual parts of documents being admitted, so we were wondering what is the case in this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is just one page that was recognised by the witness that was admitted. It is not the entire document. So I ask the Registrar to insert in the transcript that it is page 01520657, document 4086.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can you please now raise the blinds. We shall continue with examination-in-chief. Sir, good morning. I greet you on behalf of the Judges and all of those present in the courtroom. I shall now yield the floor to Mr. Mundis who will continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Again with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that we return to the issue of the bundle of photographs and the sketch map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown the photograph that formerly was bearing the number P 09587.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, do you see a photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what this building -- or what this photo is a depiction of.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a store. It is a florist's and undertaking equipment store.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, do you recognise any of the buildings in the background of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I recognise all the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what the buildings in the background of this photograph are, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the background, at the top, you can see the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there, Witness. Could you please put an S on the building that you recognise as being the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what else you can see in the background of this photo, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left there is a building housing old shops and an employment office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Place an X, please, on the buildings housing the shop and the employment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness BI. Can you see any -- or do you recognise any other buildings in the background of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the right side, there is the butcher shop, the entrance to the mosque, and a row of haberdashery shops; pastry shops, small goods shops, petty goods, such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, can you please place an M on the entrance to the mosque as visible in this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in the bottom right-hand corner can you please place the number 2 in order to identify this photograph. Number 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again just for the record, the building that you've told us was the floral shop or the florist shop, can you put an F on the building that is the floral shop.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that the map be placed back on the screen. Witness BI, do you see the floral shop indicated anywhere on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please place the number 2 at the location where the floral shop is on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd ask now that the next photograph be shown to the witness. This is the photograph that was previously P 09585. Witness BI, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what is visible in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the top, right corner, you can see the butcher shop roof, the entrance to the mosque, the eateries, about three of them, a cafe which is called Cafe Bar Roko, and the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's start again, Witness BI, by placing the number 3 in the lower right-hand corner of this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you, sir, if you could please place the letter B on the butcher shop roof.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The letter M on the entrance to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The letter S on the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You mentioned three eateries. Could you please place Xs on the three -- or the eateries.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if you could please take a look at the map. If you see, Witness, the area on that map that is depicted in photograph number 3, can you please place the number 3 on that location on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd ask now that the witness be shown the next photograph, which was previously P 09581. Witness BI, do you recognise what's shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what this is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a water fountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where is this water fountain located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the courtyard of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please, Witness BI, place the number 4 on the lower right-hand corner of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, again, if we could turn our attention to the map, if you see the fountain depicted on photograph 4 on the location of the map, please place the number 4 on the map at the corresponding location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness BI. I'd ask now that the next photograph, which was previously marked as P 09580 be shown to the witness. Witness BI, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that is, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Sultan Selim's mosque, or the emperor's, the czar's mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I neglected to ask you yesterday, do you know approximately when the Sultan Selim or the emperor, czar's mosque was built?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think - I'm not sure - that it was built in the 16th century.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please place the number 5 in the lower right-hand corner of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a minor observation to make. We can see in the photographs -- you can see typewritten in what the photograph depicts so I think it's rather silly to have a witness identify what is there for him to read already. So I don't see how we are getting anywhere. And I also don't see the relevancy of all these pictures. We don't know when they were taken, whether they are true and accurate representation prior to any incidents, and I suspect that we are going to see some photographs later, but I think we need some foundation so at least we know where we are going with this -- with all these pictures. So perhaps we can lay some foundational questions before we go into this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We will lose some time. This witness played soccer in Stolac. He is very well familiar with that town, and he certainly knows about the mosque. You asked him what was depicted on the photograph and he was able to identify it as Sultan Selim's mosque. So everything is quite logical. Mr. Mundis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can we turn again to the map. You've just marked a photograph of the Sultan Selim mosque as number 5. Can you please mark the corresponding location on the map with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness BI. Now, yesterday you described for us witnessing a fire or a number of fires in this location or in the locations of the tepa and the mosque. Can you describe for us what that area looked like after the fires were extinguished.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it looked like? Well, only the walls remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what -- can you elaborate on what you mean by "only the walls remained."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was on fire from about 3 p.m. to 8 p.m. In a word, only the basic skeletons of the buildings remained. Everything that could burn did burn, except for stone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, can you tell us, if you know, what caused the fire to go out at 8 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that it was arson. There was no shelling on that day. Very few people moved around Stolac. Only HVO troops did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time this fire was burning, did you see any of these HVO troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. During the day I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the fire brigade? Did you see the fire brigade on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask now that the witness be shown the next photograph which was marked as P 09584. Witness, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this photograph is a picture of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the eateries that I marked with an X a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when the eateries looked like this, what time period they looked like this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what time period. I suppose from the 15th to the 1st or 3rd of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what, Witness, just for the record at this point, what is significant about the 1st or 3rd of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was perhaps from the 28th of July that the persecutions of the Muslim population started, which ended, I believe, on the 3rd or 4th, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll return to that subject in just a few moments, Witness BI. Can you please for now mark this photograph as number -- with the number 6 in the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again if we can return to the map, if you can place the number 6 on the map at the corresponding location as depicted in that last photograph which you similarly marked with the number 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd ask that the following photograph, which was P 09586 be shown to the witness. Witness, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the florist'S, and in front there is a row of beauty parlours, hairdressers, cafes, and the upper part used to be a residential quarters. To the right, there used to be a children's toy shop. And this building is a row of shops and the employment office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, can you again place the letter F on the florist as depicted in this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, for the record, can you please indicate on the bottom right-hand corner this photograph by marking it with the number 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again if we can return to the map, if you can again -- the buildings depicted in photograph 7, can you mark them on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The situation as it's depicted in photograph 7, Witness, can you tell us approximately when those buildings looked as they did in photograph 7?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buildings were set on fire on the same day as the mosque. That is a period from the 15th to the 1st or 3rd, so the 15th of July to the 1st or 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Witness BI, for how long did these buildings remain in this condition? How long after that time period did these buildings remain in this condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but I know when I arrived in Stolac for the first time, these buildings were not there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you to clarify. When you say, "when I arrived in Stolac for the first time," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the organised visit to the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When, approximately, was this organised visit to the town? We'll go back into this subject in a few moments, but approximately when was this organised visit to the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in 1995 or 1996. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask now that the witness be shown the last photograph in this bundle, which was P 09588. Witness, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what is depicted in this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the school, the Cafe Bar Roko, with residential quarters, and to the right side you can see the remnants, the ruins that we marked on sketch number 1, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, sir, can you please place the letter S on the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the letter R on the Cafe Bar Roko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please place an X on the remnants or ruins that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, just again for the record, can we mark this photograph with the number 8 in the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you know approximately when or do you have a rough idea as to when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was between 1993 and 1995 or 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, this large area at the bottom, say bottom half of this photograph which we marked with the number 8, what previously was in this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mosque -- all the previous images that we explained; the mosque, the butcher's, the eateries, the florist's, the shops, the residential quarters, all those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please, Witness BI, mark with the letter M the approximate location where the Sultan Selim mosque formerly stood.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what this area was used for after the war or in more recent times, this area where you've marked with the M.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, after the Bosniaks returned, this area wasn't used for anything; it was overgrown in weeds. And once the Bosniaks cleared it all up, this area was mostly used as a parking lot. The municipality built a parking lot here, and the mosque was rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Witness BI, approximately when the mosque was rebuilt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mosque was rebuilt, I believe, from 2002 to late 2004 or early 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the tepa? Has the tepa been rebuilt in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But this area that we previously marked with an X on the front part is privately owned. This wall that you can see here. Most of this area is privately owned, and most of it was renewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that these nine photographs and map be bundled together and be given an In Court identification number and tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, please give us the number of all the photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... assigned the reference IC 00018. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, I have just a few more questions for you and these concern the events from this period commencing on or about either 1 or 3 August, 1993. Can you tell us, Witness BI, what happened to you on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that on that day, in the morning, early in the morning, between 7 and 8.30 a.m., four soldiers came to the door of my house. They wore the HVO insignia. They asked us to get the most basic belongings and to go to the playground of the elementary school. We did as we were told. We went to the playground of the elementary school where we found a large number of the residents of Stolac, predominantly Bosniaks or Muslims. It were all -- it was all women, children, the elderly, disabled people. After that, when the playground was full, they would take ten to 20 people at a time to the school, to the school building. They searched them there, confiscated money, jewellery, gold, all other valuables. For example, if you had three bags on you, they would throw away two of them and leave you with just one. After leaving the classrooms, we would go to the front part of the school where a truck was waiting for us. They would board us on trucks and take us what Blagaj from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness BI, let me ask you a couple of follow-on questions. You said on page 13, line 2, that there were a large number of the residents of Stolac. Do you recall approximately how many people were gathered at this playground of the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we learned later, this playground was not the only collection point, gathering point. The playground itself is not large; perhaps 250 to 300 people can fit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what about your apartment when you left the apartment? Can you tell us about the condition of your apartment when you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our apartment was not in great condition. It had been damaged by shrapnel, shells, and so on, but these were minor things. The damage was minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us a few moments ago that you later discovered that there were other collection centres in Stolac. Do you recall or can you tell us a little bit about where these other locations were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The building of the VP centre, the building of the ironworks, or the building of the construction reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, again, for the benefit of the record, can you tell us what the VP centre was, or what that -- the initials VP stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the building of the correctional facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And correctional facility for whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, the juvenile delinquents were held there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So it was a facility for juveniles, it wasn't a full-blown prison for adults?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness BI, you told us that they -- on this is on line 10 of page 13 -- "They would board us on trucks and take us to Blagaj from there." Can you tell us a little bit about what happened at Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Blagaj. I don't remember how we travelled from Stolac, because the truck was enclosed. I only remember when we got to the Buna, they opened up the truck, we got off, and the HVO soldiers started directing us to where we had to go. It was a narrow road where there were anti-tank mines. We had to pass through the mines and go down to Blagaj. Upon reaching Blagaj, we were met by some army units and units of the civilian protection. They put us into vacant Serb and Croat houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I intervene? Witness BI, you have said that the lorry on which you were transported was, the word used here is "enclosed" and you didn't see anything. How, then, do you know or where do you get the information that there were mines on the road you were taking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You misunderstood me, sir. I didn't see anything until we got to the Buna. Once we reached Buna, we got off the truck. They took us off the truck, and then we walked on foot for the rest of the trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise if I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, approximately how far is it that you walked from Buna to Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think approximately seven to eight kilometres. It was very hot and the road seemed much longer. It was difficult to walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how long did it take you to walk from Buna to Blagaj on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately three hours. The road is quite narrow and there were many people. The columns were big. There were many corpses on the road, so some three to three and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how many people went with you on this walk from Buna to Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the exact number. I don't know it. But I assume that there were between 800 and 1.000 people on that day on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, do you know where these people, these 800 to 1.000 people that were on the road that day with you, where were these people from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 99.9 per cent of them were from Stolac. As for the remaining 0.1 per cent, I think those were the remaining residents from Dubrave, because people had been driven out of Dubrave a day or two before we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, how long did you remain in Blagaj after you arrived there on that day in August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent less than an hour in Blagaj. I was then transferred to Dracevica, which is where I lived until I returned to Stolac. I'm not sure about the year. It was 1995 or 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where, Witness, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, where is Dracevica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a small place on the road leading to Nevesinje, on one side, and on the other side, you can say that it's located between Blagaj and Mostar. Or to be more specific, it is exactly across the Mostar airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, can you tell the Trial Chamber about the first time you returned to Stolac after leaving in August of 1993. Tell us about the circumstances in which you first returned to Stolac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you a bit ago, the first time I came to Stolac, it was an organised visit. There were two buses, and it was organised by the then government in Stolac, which was in Mostar. This visit was hindered in all possible ways. The first two or three attempts to enter Stolac failed, and once we did manage to enter Stolac after the intervention of SFOR, which was the then UFOR, the local police treated us as we were some sort of hooligans. I'm not sure how to call this. They held us in an enclosed area and there was -- we were cordoned off by policemen. And this is how we walked through the town. We couldn't go to the left or the right or where we wanted; we had to go where they took us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness BI, do you recall the approximate time period when you went with this organised visit in these two buses back to Stolac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1995 or 1996. I'm not sure. At any rate, it was hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is outside the indictment period. I don't see what the relevance is to this other than to try to inflame the passions of professional Judges, which as we all know, doesn't occur, or at least is not supposed to, or at least I'm told it doesn't happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Mundis, why is this relevant, this question, namely to say that the witness came back to his town in 1995 or 1996?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It simply completes the witness's narrative as to the events of what happened to him, Mr. President, and also explains the results of the alleged criminal activity described in the indictment. This does complete the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to lodge another objection in regards to that last comment, Your Honour. There was a war going on in that country, people were dislodged from all over the place, and I think it's an unfair characterisation for the Prosecutor to try to sneak in this sort of stuff at the end of the examination. It's totally irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness BI, I will need several minor clarifications. You said that you walked from Buna to Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, as far as you can remember -- it's been many years, I understand that you can't remember everything, but during your march, during your walk, did you hear any shots fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But they didn't shoot directly at the people. At least, nobody got killed. They fired in order to intimidate us, to make us walk faster. Mostly the bullets zoomed above our heads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They fired from behind us, from behind our backs. That is to say the soldiers who remained in Buna, who had held positions in the forest and Kicin and other places. I'm not sure what these places are called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So you say that the soldiers who were in Buna fired above your heads as you were walking towards Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I put this question because in the indictment it is mentioned that fire was opened while people were marching. Another question: When the fire was set to the mosque, to the florist shop and other facilities that you mentioned to us, were you personally present there at the spot? Did you see these fires with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At what time did the fire start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the afternoon hours, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were you in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I stated yesterday, I was with my friends, Croat friends. We were playing soccer at the playground behind the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So you were playing soccer, and at that moment you saw the fire. What drew your attention to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not while I was playing soccer. I didn't see the fire then. As I was walking home from the playground, I saw in the courtyard of the mosque a lot of smoke, so I entered the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you didn't see the people who started the fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were there any other residents who were there, on the spot, as this was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps there were two to three boys, Croats. Two or three, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And nobody said who set the fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Witness BI one question. When you describe your marching from Buna to Blagaj, you mentioned that it was a rather long trip and although it was only about eight to nine kilometres but the marching on was rather slow. And during this time, you have also seen a number of corpses along the road. So I would like to ask you when you referred to the corpse, that is dead persons most probably, what was there -- I mean, they were not in a way buried, and what was the cause, in your view, of their being there without any burying? This is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people who were dead, lying dead on the road, were predominantly the elderly, those who were weak, exhausted, sick, and couldn't take such heat, 40 to 45 degrees. Perhaps they also lacked water. At any rate, they couldn't survive that trip. Perhaps they were even ill. Mostly they were the elderly and the ill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: A small question: You have said that when you were shot at, or above your heads, no one was killed. Was, to your knowledge, anybody injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution used up one hour -- one and a half hours for examination-in-chief, but I think that another Judge has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness BI, you explained to us what was going on in the morning, either on the 1st or 3rd of August, 1993, you said between 7 and 8 in the morning, when four HVO soldiers came to your house in order to take you to the school building. You told us who was in the school building. You said that there were many residents, Muslim residents, of Stolac gathered there. My question for you is this: Can you confirm or can you be more specific in telling us whether that morning some kind of a raid was organised? Were people rounded up and was this operation directed exclusively against the Muslims? And if so, please tell us, how did the members of the HVO organise themselves in order to recognise those who were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not the only one who can answer this question. Various TV stations were taping a programme several years ago with Croats from Stolac who were describing the events of that morning, and these Croats said, "That morning we got up earlier," meaning earlier than the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now I will yield the floor to the Defence. You have a total of hour and a half available to you. I don't know who is going to begin. I don't know whether you have reached an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will begin. I have a few questions. I shouldn't take more than a few moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to touch on a couple of issues. The first issue, I guess, is on the shelling of Stolac. You indicated yesterday that the Serbs had been shelling Stolac but you didn't go into any great detail. I would like you to kind of describe for us where exactly the shelling was and the damage.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs entered Stolac in 1991. They were continuously passing through Stolac, going to Dubrave, Capljina, Metkovici. I don't know where their positions were. They withdrew from Stolac once the HVO entered, and the HOS. I think that it was in 1992. They withdrew to the positions around Stolac, in Zebulja, Hrgut, Bancici. And from there, initially, from the beginning of the war, they shelled Stolac intensely, and then gradually the shelling was reduced until the Muslims were expelled or, rather, the Muslim residents were taken to camps and it was then that the shelling stopped completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And these were Serbs shelling Stolac? These were Serbs shelling Stolac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that continued all the way until 1993? May, June, July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say up until May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, obviously you were too young to participate in any military activity, but are you aware that members of the HVO were Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what about HOS, HOS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the HVO -- HOS, I remember when they entered Stolac. These were mostly not local people. There were, at most, four or five residents of Stolac who were members of HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were they Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But Muslims by religion. They felt they were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, could you explain that a little bit? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They acted like Croats. They were more Croats than proper Croats. They conducted themselves as proper Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just to go back, when you said May in my earlier question, the shelling, that was May, 1993, correct? I just want to clarify that point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just a couple of other questions. I was somewhat curious in the way you began yesterday, indicating the events in Stolac as they exist today, and you used a particular word, "apartheid," which is a rather unusual word, and I must say since 1999 in my experience in the entire region I've never heard that word being used before. Was that a conversation that you had with the professor before coming here today regarding Stolac and how it seemed like an apartheid situation there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That wasn't the result of the conversation with the Professor. If you were to go to Stolac now, completely irrespective of this, if you were to meet a Muslim resident of Stolac and start up a conversation with him or her, I think that 99 per cent of residents of Stolac would tell you the same thing I said to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the mayor is a Croat in Stolac today, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the president of the Assembly, is he a Croat or is he a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I've been so disappointed by politics that I lost interest in it. It makes no difference. Whoever is in power in Stolac, the situation remains the same. People do nothing, there are no jobs, so I'm not interested in who is the head of this or that office. It's all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, there are no factories working in Stolac at the moment, right? Even though, as I understand it, there either originate from Zenica, which is predominantly Muslim town, or Sarajevo, which again is a predominantly Muslim town, or Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of state-owned firms in Stolac, currently operating are the municipality, two health centres, divided into the Bosniak and the Croat health centre, two bus stations, the Bosniak and the Muslim. The only place where everything is mixed is the MUP. There you have Croats and Serbs and Muslims. As far as the factories are concerned, they have been privatised -- 90 per cent of them have been privatised, the owners being Croats. None of them is operating except for the ironworks, which perhaps employs from the pre-war number of 800, about 50 employees, workers, rather, and all of them are of Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The municipality, however, is mixed, and as you well know, because of OHR running the country more or less, everything has to be advertised.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, for instance, if you are above me, can my signature mean anything without yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question. But needless to say, everything that -- all the jobs are advertised publicly and everything is scrutinised and transparent as a result of OHR being there to ensure that there is no discrimination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, talking about OHR, they actually forget about Stolac in 90 per cent of the cases, as a matter of fact. That is actually the last thing on their mind, in terms of importance, on this planet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next Defence team? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I only have a few brief questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness BI. I represent General Praljak. I'm a lawyer from Rijeka. I would just like to clarify certain things that you have already said which do not appear clear when reading the transcript. You described the situation in Stolac after the HVO had liberated Stolac, but I believe that nothing has been said about the position of the HVO lines facing the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to those lines. I did after the war, but as far as I know, on the basis of what I was told by the soldiers who went to the lines, they faced Ljubina, Basilije and Poplat. They were in that direction, and they were in the direction of Berkovici. There was the Osanici line right above Stolac itself. Then there was Komanje hill, and I think there was a line in Begovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm particularly interested in Begovina and the line facing the Chetniks along the edge of Begovina. That was the line that was closest to the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the lines in Basilije and Poplat were closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. In a certain sense, the war and the defence lines were a daily occurrence; they were there at the edge of the town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Serbian shelling that you have mentioned, how frequent was this? How frequently did they shell the area? Was it more frequent in June or July of 1993 or was the shelling more frequent later on? I apologise; in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually 20 or 30 shells would fall on Stolac. I remember that on one day, the 15th of August, 1992, there was an attack and the shelling lasted throughout the day. The shelling lasted throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did the inhabitants take shelter then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly they were in the cellars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the HVO and the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go out on that day. I couldn't even leave the house. I have no idea as to what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In your assessment, and I think you mentioned May and July, it wasn't quite clear, but in your assessment, what would you say? You would say -- would you say that at one period of time the shelling by the Chetniks decreased but it nevertheless continued. When did the intensity of the shelling diminish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how should I put it? Perhaps from May onwards, when they took the men away to the camps, at that point in time the shelling had ceased completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, at the time of these events, if my calculations were correct, you were 13 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And 13 years have passed since those events occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So that was mid -- at the mid-point in your life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: However, you remember certain things quite precisely. You could mention certain dates and months, give or take a couple of weeks. However, the Prosecution asked you today about certain events that occurred later on, and I will quote what you said from the transcript. First, you were asked about the mark number 7 on the photograph, about the photograph marked with number 7. You were asked when the objects looked the way they looked in the photograph, and you said that those buildings had been set on fire on the same day as the mosque. So that was between the 15th and the -- of July and the 3rd of August. And at the beginning of your testimony you said it was during those 15 days that these events transpired. And then immediately after that, the Prosecution asked you how long the buildings remained in that state, and you answered, "I can't remember exactly but I know that when I arrived in Stolac for the first time -" so that's when you returned there to visit the town - "the buildings were still there." And when you were asked when you returned for the first time, you said it was in 1995 or in 1996. In order to assess your memory, I have to put this question to you: When you refer to 1993, you can be precise within a two-week period, more or less. When you talk about something that occurred two years later, and this has to do with your experiences, with your emotions, too, because it was the first time you returned to your birth place, when you talk about such events, you can no longer say exactly whether it was in 1995 or 1996, so you're not even sure of the exact year, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I'm not sure. However, I'd like to correct something. A minute ago, when you mentioned these buildings in photograph number 7, I don't know how this was interpreted but I didn't say that they were still there when I first returned to Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. There is some other sentence here but the period of time is important.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I experienced something that is difficult to imagine so I wouldn't even know what I had to eat the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I agree. Perhaps there is one other matter that I would like to clarify. You mentioned the civilians, you civilians being sent down the road from Buna to Blagaj, they opened fire above your heads, in order to hurry you up, send you in the right direction. You said that there were some tank mines on that road too. In order to understand the situation completely, were the tank mines visible obstacles and were there these hedgehogs on the road too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the road from Buna to Blagaj, I believe that there was one so-called hedgehog in front of them. But the mines were laid on a 200- to 300-metre stretch of road, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But those tank mines were visible, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So what I'm trying to say is that they hadn't been concealed, as is the case with a trip-wire mines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but they were visible, just like this jug here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You say that there was one line of mines that had been marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not one line. On the road from Buna to Blagaj, well, let's say the mines were here, the hedgehog was in front. But at the end of the line of mines, there was no hedgehog. That's quite logical. They placed that obstacle there for their soldiers, to prevent someone from going astray.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: While you were passing through, were there any casualties as the result of the mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We walked along the other side. The path was about as wide as this table here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned Blagaj, who met you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian protection and the BH army. We met some troops there who were at the lines, I think that the place is called Kosor. They directed us to Blagaj, and when we arrived at the entrance to Blagaj, there were perhaps 20 or 30 people from the civilian protection. There were elderly people, and they provided us with accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this road between Buna and Blagaj, this was a no man's land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We'll have to repeat that because we were overlapping. We have to repeat that because of the transcript. So this was a no-man's land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the demarcation line. Six or seven kilometres along -- or of those six or seven kilometres that I mentioned, three represented the no man's land.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I have one more question, although I don't think it's very relevant. Something was entered into the transcript unnecessarily so I would like to correct that. On page 16 or 15, my colleague intervened. You were asked about that first visit to Stolac in 1995 and 1996, and you mentioned certain abbreviations. I'm not sure whether everyone is familiar with those abbreviations. They weren't clearly stated. You said that the visit was organised by SFOR or what was then called UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that it was organised by the Stolac government. The visit was organised by the Stolac government. People who had organised themselves in Mostar. And we couldn't enter Stolac without an escort. On two or three occasions we were sent back from Buna, and then SFOR, or UNPROFOR, what is now called OFOR and then it was called SFOR, they made it possible for us to pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So SFOR were foreign forces. They weren't local forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think they were foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And they made it possible for you to pass through?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The two speakers were overlapping, the interpreter could not hear what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]. Thank you, Your Honour. I only have five minutes. I only need five minutes, no longer than that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, when you arrived in Blagaj, you said that you were put up in Croatian houses. Where were the Croats who lived in Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Luksa forest. You're well aware of the fact.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Please, answer my question. Do you know where the Croats were, whose houses were used for your accommodation when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved into a Muslim house myself but there were Bosniak families who lived in Croatian and Serbian houses, whereas the Croats were on the other side of the -- of the -- of the runway, as you well know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In 1992, the Serbs entered Stolac and most of the inhabitants, first Croatian inhabitants and then the Serbian inhabitants, and then the Muslim inhabitants, left that area. According to the information that we'll show to the Court, 10.000 Bosniaks then crossed the Neretva River and moved over to the right side. In June, 1992, the HOS and the HVO liberated Stolac. How is it that at that time, there was peace, a kind of understanding, and even love between the Croats and the Muslims? Why were mosques not set on fire at the time? Why were houses not torched? And how is it that it's only one year later that the events you have described actually occurred? The events that you have truthfully described. What happened during that year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were all equal. They all had rifles. I did just as you did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes. That rifle that had been provided to the Bregava Brigade certainly wasn't provided by the Serbian side, it was provided by the Croatian side. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't participate in the war. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that in the meantime, during that one-year period, a war was raging throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina? Do you know what happened in the spring of 1993 in Konjic, in Kakanj, in Travnik, in Sarajevo? Can you see any connections between all of these events? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a political sense, but I can't just say yes or no. Allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't say "thank you," let me explain this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I understand this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was obvious for the Serbs to finish their work in Bosnia. I can even mention the names of the Croats who came to live in Stolac from Kakanj, Kraljeva and Sutjeska, and they cursed themselves for having done that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, I think they will talk about these matters on the basis of other documents before this Court. Have you ever seen me or any of these other five accused setting houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know you because I've seen you on television.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Please, we don't have much time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you see any orders in which it said that you should set houses on fire and take people away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think commands -- I think the troops should be in barracks. I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. With regard to the Croatian and Serbian agreement, how is it that after the liberation of Stolac on the 15th of August, the Serbs wanted to take Stolac and launch a significant attack, if there was an agreement about the division of territory between the Croats and the Serbs? Do you have an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what your position was, I think it was a military position. When the HVO and HOS entered --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, how many shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One bomb, one shell was fired, and the Serbs left Stolac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You know this or you knew this at the age of 13?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could see that with my very own eyes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. It's unusual that you say that the people and you yourself spent most of your time in the cellars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I understand. On the 15th of August, in particular, you spent that day in the cellars and nevertheless you know what people who were not in the cellars looked like, you knew what the fight or the battle looked like, you know how many bullets had been shot and how many shells had been launched.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the 15th of August. I'm talking about the HVO and when they entered Stolac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. If you were in the vicinity of the fires themselves, there were other -- and there were other people there, how is it that no one recognised those who set these buildings on fire? How is it that so many eye-witnesses have hidden or how is it that no one reported them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean the eye-witnesses hid?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I mean that those who set the buildings on fire hid from the eye-witnesses. No one could see them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, have you seen the photographs? Have you seen the footage? Let me explain how it is possible not to see them. Have you seen the footage? Have you seen the footage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've seen that everything went in a circle. If it was on fire here, the first fire broke out here. Let's say in front of me, perhaps 20 metres away from me. I would put the fire out. Five minutes later, photograph number 1 was burning on the other side, or what was shown in photograph number 1 was burning on the other side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I understand you. Completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak is putting an important question to you, which follows on from what I wanted to ask you about. Mr. Praljak is asking the following question: You were there. There were other persons too. But after the event, no one said who set the buildings on fire. That's the question put to you. What could you tell us about that? Because you said there was a sort of circular movement; when you put the fire out at one location, some other building was put -- was set fire to at another place. Let's say that's correct. You were in Stolac on that day and there were other people there. After the fires, did the inhabitants say or did they tell you about the identity of those who had set these buildings on fire, and were they arrested? That's the question that's been put to you. You can either answer it or not. But please stay calm. It's not necessary to get excited when a question is put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. I don't think soldiers will speak against themselves. The identity of those who set these buildings on fire was never discovered. While all these buildings were on fire, they were perhaps 20 metres away, on the steps in front of the school, and they were laughing, shooting into the air, and doing all sorts of other things. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But try to understand this: I am to be held accountable. There were eye-witnesses but there are many people, there are a lot of people who can't identify a single person who set these buildings on fire. No one can be asked whether someone issued an order, an oral or a written order, to set these buildings on fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not for me to address this issue. But I think that the there is a sufficient number of people in Stolac who know who set their house on fire or who set something valuable on fire. I don't know the identity of these people. I didn't see anyone taking a match, dousing a building with petrol and setting it on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Don't you think that it would be important for the Court to have information about this? If there were people who knew about the identity of the perpetrators, don't you think they would have gone to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that would have been realistic, but given the situation in Stolac, that's -- that would have been impossible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I want to ask you something about apartheid. You're a law graduate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I graduated two years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: From 1996 onwards, how many elections have been held in Stolac, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Elections were held perhaps on one or two occasions, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Elections have been held in Stolac on four occasions since 1996. They were all held under the auspices of the international community. Do you think that democratically held elections, having the right to be elected, having the right to participate in public life, can such things be called apartheid in the legal sense of the term? I understand your emotions, but please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well in legal terms it wouldn't be realistic to describe these matters in such terms. But go and live in Stolac for a while and you'll see what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have one more question for you. At the ruins of the mosque that was set on fire, the remains of an old Catholic church appeared; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So where were the ruins of an old Catholic church found? Which mosque was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if ruins had been found, I think a church would have been built there, not a mosque, but the churches you're referring to aren't Catholic ones, they are Orthodox ones.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Bisko -- that Mr. Peric suggested that a mosque be built right the next to a church and that they have a common wall so as to interrupt the series of acts of destruction against religious buildings. But thank you very much. I have no more questions. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's 10.30 now. We will have our technical break and we'll resume in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We are resuming our hearing in order to finish with the cross-examination, but before Mrs. Alaburic takes the floor, let me tell you, sir: Please try to answer as briefly as possible by saying yes or no to the questions, and please keep your calm. Don't let anything upset you. The lawyers are just doing their job. So I now give the floor to Mrs. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of General Petkovic has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will have a few questions for the witness, and Mr. Coric possibly also. It is just a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. BI, I am Tomislav Jonjic. I shall ask you a few questions on behalf of Mr. Coric. You described for us the liberation of Stolac, the entry of HVO and HOS units into Stolac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, irrespective of the fact that you were young at the time - but we can see that your memory is quite good - can you remember, in the weeks and the months that ensued after the liberation of Stolac, did the Croats who had fled during the Serbian occupation, as well as the Muslims, did they return or did this process evolve only slowly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croats, most of the Croats returned, but the male population, the part of the population that was prepared to bear arms, in other words, were as a rather large number of Muslims, returned with their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Was this return attended by any difficulties? Did the authorities, those that had the actual power in the city at that time, create any difficulties for them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In returning?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell us, today you mentioned that quite a few, there were quite a few Muslims in the HOS, and you used a formulation which I find slightly peculiar, so would you be so kind as to explain. Namely, you said that the Muslims in HOS, that they pretended to be truer Croats than real Croats. That's page 23.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what this is about? Does this mean that a Muslim cannot feel to be a Croat in the ethnic and national sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that in your book a person of Muslim faith cannot feel to be a Croat in the national, ethnic sense; or if he does feel that, is he considered a traitor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Observed from today's standpoint, a person of Muslim ethnicity that feels to be a Croat is a traitor, in my book, and I believe that such people were actually seeking to score points for their account, pretending, feigning to be Croats, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: So in your view, there is an identity between ethnic affiliation and religious affiliation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we show the witness, with the aid of the Registry, document for which the Defence of Mr. Coric was not originally prepared because the subject had not been referred to in the statement of Witness BI but it has cropped up as potentially important and relevant in the cross-examination, and this is document Defence of Mr. Stojic, which is in the e-court under number 2D 00022, and which was submitted immediately prior to the beginning of this session to the Trial Chamber and to us. Can we have that document shown, please. Well, if you cannot see it in the electronic system, then we have a copy for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: This document has several pages. Of course, we have a translation into English also. Of relevance is just the first page, in fact, because the rest of the pages are just names. So to assist the witness and save some time, this is a document of the Croatian Defence Council of the 15th of June, 1993, and it enumerates, or rather, its enclosure submits a list of 314 families that, according to this document, are -- were expelled, had been expelled by Muslim extremists from their family homes in Kocina, Gnojnica, Dracevica, Malo Polje, Blagaj, and other villages. So these are Croatian families that we are talking about. In this connection I should like to ask the witness: Are these villages in which the families that moved from Stolac through Buna to the Blagaj area were accommodated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this be admitted into the file as an exhibit, Defence Exhibit, for Mr. Coric? And today we shall see to it that it also is included in the electronic system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This exhibit has already been admitted for Mr. Stojic and will be so for you. Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is important that it be tendered into the file. Whether under the existing mark or another one, that is not important.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification: I mean such occurrences, while the system can accommodate such occurrences, we just need to have -- to be provided with the next sequential number of your Defence team, starting with 5D 000 whatever. This is a standard procedure. So if you give me the next sequential number, I can admit it as such. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. While we are waiting, do you have the number? Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. 5D 01080 is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Registrar, please give us the number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will therefore be assigned the reference 5D 01080, and for the record, this is the very same document as the one submitted by the 2D Defence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: My last question for this witness today: You mentioned that in your view, it was only the MUP, the civilian police, in Stolac that was functioning as a joint institution, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know as of which date, as of when, the civil police was functioning in that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From perhaps two and a half to three years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Not before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the same building, actually, but there were no powers vested in the Muslims. In fact, a policeman in the first day after our return, a policeman in uniform was actually reluctant to go out in the street lest he meet with some discomfort.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Who was the minister at the moment of the establishment of the joint police, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Coric, please put your questions now. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will have a couple of very brief questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: You said that you did not recall the name nor knew the name of a single person who took part in the setting on fire of buildings and the mosque in Stolac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct and nobody asked me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you. Can you tell me a single name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you the name of some of the soldiers who were on the staircase, on the stairs: Marijan --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Tell me one name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marijan Prce.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the persons who arrested you when you were moving out of Stolac, when you had to go outside the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But no, but I remember the persons who frisked us, who took our gold and our money.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in names. It is important that you know who they were. Do you remember the name of the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: My next question: Do you know whether any of those persons has been tried before courts in Bosnia-Herzegovina so far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, some are on the run, some are at large. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: But have some been indicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Can you say some names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marijan Prce, Vide Palameta, and I can't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any procedures are underway for over a year now against some persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see that you are acquainted with the situation in Stolac now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Over these past few years, did you or some of the people in Stolac that experienced what you had gone through, did you report to the official organs or launch a criminal complaint against any of the persons who participated in these actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is no need for that at all because at the very entrance to the MUP there are All Points Bulletins on the wall for these persons that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: So they have been actually subjected to this procedure, don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talk about the MUP, I was the MUP minister when the joint police was formed in the Herzegovina Neretva canton, meaning also in Stolac. Do you know that the functions of the most responsible persons, that the duties were divided on an ethnic basis so you knew who was the head of the police, who was the deputy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know, but I know that now if the head was a Croat, his deputy would be a Muslim. That is actually the current situation. I know that that is the current situation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. During your first visit to Stolac, you said that you were secured by a cordon of the police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: What police was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Stolac police. They had black belts with this white patch, white patch where it was written the Stolac HZ Police Herceg-Bosna; you know that circular patch.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
