utterances.text: And now my question: Is Exhibit P 02586 a letter that you sent to Mr. M. Petkovic and Mr. J. Topic, requesting a cease-fire in recognition or celebration of Bajram?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you sign that letter, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, was a cease-fire granted or allowed by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: No cease-fire was allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What happened in connection with the celebration of this holiday?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: We were in a situation to celebrate it -- we weren't in a situation to celebrate it publicly. If it was possible to do it privately in one's own home, that was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you next about the treatment of Islamic church officials during this time, in the spring and summer, perhaps fall, of 1993. Can you tell us whether any Islamic clerics or officials were arrested and detained by the HVO during this time period?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: It's true that many members of our clergy were treated in an extremely brutal way. They were taken to concentration camps where they were treated in the worst possible way. In my area, 14 imams, 14 members of the clergy, were taken to these camps and they suffered various forms of brutal maltreatment. I can particularly underline the example of the Tuzla mufti. I can emphasise this example. A week before a fierce strike was carried out against Mostar and Herzegovina on the 2nd of May, 1993, he was arrested in Konjic by HVO units. Although he had regular papers from the HVO in Mostar, he was returning from Croatia, he was intercepted at that check-point. Although he had appropriate papers, he was detained for seven months under extremely difficult conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask the witness to be shown Exhibit P 09559. And, sir, did you previously prepare a list of the names of 12 Islamic clerics, imams, who, based on your knowledge, were arrested and detained by the HVO during 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I submitted this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is the list that you have in front of you now, which is marked as Exhibit 09559, that list?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: That's the list, but these imams are from my area. My colleague from Tuzla, Imam Kavazovic, on the way from Zagreb to Mostar, via Konjic, was arrested, and he's not on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps another one not listed, perhaps you can help us with that, did anything happen to an imam named Musan Becirevic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Becirevic, Musan. He was an imam in Buna, near Mostar. He's not in this list. He was brutally killed. His family witnessed that crime and they have testified that HVO units forced Musan Becirevic to pray in front of them and, after he had done this, they brutally killed him. They did this in a mosque that they subsequently destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One of the persons on your list is Ibrahim Zlomustika [phoen] -- sorry, it's different on the list. But what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Ibrahim Zlomusica. He was an imam in Stolac. He was also humiliated and tortured in a terrible way. They tied him up in the Kostana hospital in Stolac. They used steel rope, they hung him from the ceiling, and they beat him with wooden batons, and to this very day, you can see the bruises on his face. His ribs were broken, his teeth were broken, as well as his jaw. So after he had been beaten in this way, he spent a number of months, and I have the precise information on this, I have precise information as to when the person was taken in and released, but I didn't have this information when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, about also anything that happened to another imam named -- which is on your list, number 12, Kazim Mezit.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Kasim Mezit was already dead. He didn't die in the concentration camp, in the camp. Later he was released although his health had suffered. He had been tortured by Croatian soldiers who, for reasons unknown to us, expressed their anger by beating him in particular, so several years afterwards, he died. I've testified more about this individual in the Tuta case, but if you need any additional information, I'm prepared to provide you with it. Mr. Tuta treated him in a special way. He took him to Siroki Brijeg. He forced him to sign some kind of statement that he provided him with, and when he refused to sign this statement, Mr. Tuta took the pencil he had given him, and the piece of paper, and he stuck the pencil into his face, and the pencil penetrated his cheeks. It went right through both cheeks. And he was also maltreated in other ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, before I turn to the last topic, cultural destruction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would first like to ask the registrar to inform me of the time that has been used up so far. Please continue, Mr. Scott. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we leave the imams and the Islamic clerics that -- some of them that you were involved in, let me ask you this: In your position or role as a mufti, have you ever been involved in the appointment of someone to a position called an Emir - and if I mispronounce that, my apology - in a military unit. An Emir.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: That only happened on one occasion. There was a small group of people who were part of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, from the military point of view, but they requested that their internal and intimate life be organised in a somewhat different manner. This concerned about 50 men who noticed that there were men in army units who would drink alcohol and would behave in various ways, and they wanted to organise their lives to the extent that this was possible in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Islamic moral code. And as a result, Mr. Pasalic, the Commander of the 4th Corps, told me reluctantly, that we needed each and every soldier, although we wanted to establish an army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not a Muslim army, so he said that they should be organised in this manner because he had seen other such groups organised in territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he asked me to appoint one person whom we trusted, as some sort of assistant for morale, something like that, and that was in fact done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would this be -- would such a position or person be something that might be considered in Western armies as a chaplain?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in terms of religious or cultural destruction, can you tell us what you experienced and observed during your time in Mostar in the summer and fall of 1993, in terms of what you learned about the destruction of particularly mosques and other Islamic cultural sites.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostar was a kind of Hiroshima.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we didn't hear the question [Microphone not activated] We didn't hear the question because the microphone is not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's not working, Your Honour. I'm sorry, I can't have any -- now it's on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, to repeat my question, can you tell us what you experienced and observed during your time in Mostar in the summer and fall of 1993 in terms of what you learned about the destruction of particular mosque -- in particular mosques and other Islamic cultural sites.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: All the buildings that belonged to the Islamic community, the mosques and not only religious buildings but also residential buildings and cultural buildings, anything that had oriental connotations or had an appearance that made it possible to identify them as part of the Bosnian Islamic culture, all such buildings were constantly targeted and destroyed. There is not a single mosque in town that wasn't destroyed. In 1994, and I won't provide you with the individual examples, particular examples. In 1994, when the first delegation arrived on behalf of the Islamic community, on behalf of the Presidency, after the Dayton Agreement had been signed in March, well, we didn't have a single mosque in which we could pray. So they had been completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: After the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, not even the old bridge went unscathed. So these were buildings that were deliberately targeted. And infantry weapons were also used to inflict damage on these buildings, because they were mosques at the demarcation line. And snipers targeted them. Day in and day out. They were destroyed, these buildings, stone by stone. And that is proof that this destruction was inflicted in a systematic way and the purpose of the destruction was to transform a normal and multi-ethnic and multi-religious town into a town that belonged to only the members of one particular culture and that belonged to one people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you inform the Judges whether there was any Islamic church policy, religious policy, about whether any mosque or other religious buildings or facilities could be used, as far as the church was concerned, as a military position?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: I categorically reject the suggestion that any of the religious buildings were used for any military purposes whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me come back to that. That specifically was my question: Can you tell, was it the policy of your church that they not be used, of your religion, that they not be used for such purposes?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Of course it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now -- excuse me. Let me ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P 08939. And while that's being done, sir, can you tell the Judges, did you become involved at some point in preparing a report about the destruction or damage of Islamic religious or cultural sites during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: There were numerous international and local associations that asked us to gather data on the number of religious buildings destroyed. And we compiled such reports for various purposes. When drafting this report, this procedure was initiated. The procedure the purpose of which was to determine the responsibility of the perpetrators, to identify the perpetrators. So the purpose of this report was not to provide a court with such report. We drafted it for certain institutions that were supposed to carry out an investigation and to specify exactly how many buildings had been destroyed, the extent of the damage inflicted. So that's the report from 1999, and it concerns the entire territory of the area I'm responsible for. It was based on the various municipalities, and we specified which buildings had been destroyed by the Serbian forces, which ones had been destroyed by the Croatian forces. We tried to determine the extent of the damage to determine how many religious buildings had been completely destroyed, how many mosques had been destroyed, and medzlis. There were other flats that belonged to the Islamic community and business premises that haven't been included in this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And you've previously indicated that there -- that two corrections should be made to your report. And I'm going to give you the chance to do that. If you can turn to section V, item number 3, which I know is page 5 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: That's not necessary for me to see that version. I know this by heart, so we can save time. Well, here it is now. The mosque concerned is in Livno, and under item 3 it says the mosques destroyed, there was a mosque in Grborez, if you noticed that, and it says that it was destroyed after the signing of the Dayton Agreement. That's a mistake. I went to see all the mosques. It wasn't destroyed, it was damaged. Machine-gun fire was opened on the mosque, so it wasn't destroyed. And then in the area of Tomislavgrad, in the settlement of Suica, I think it says in military action, and I amended that. There was no military action in Suica that involved the Muslims and Croats. That mosque was blown up. So that case should just be described in more precise terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: For the record, I believe you're referring to section VII, item number 1 under demolished mosque, and you would correct -- the report currently says it was demolished during the fighting and can you tell us again for the record, how would you change that statement, how would you correct that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I want to be precise. Here we have Tomislavgrad, Suica, under number 1, the mosque in the settlement of Suica was destroyed in the course of combat operations. Let me be quite precise. There were no combat operations in the area. The mosque had been deliberately destroyed but there was no conflict between the Muslims and the Croats as a result of which this building was destroyed in the course of the fighting, and that is the amendment I wanted to make. There were no military operations there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you to turn to -- to be provided or displayed the last page of your report, and in the English version, if the last page could be displayed also, please. Can you just briefly describe what this -- doesn't have it yet. If it's faster, we can put a hard copy on the ELMO, perhaps. If we could have the ELMO displayed, please. While we are doing this, Mufti Smajkic, just to save time, can you just tell us what this schedule or table is and what that indicates in general terms.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: This is the table of destroyed facilities, classified by municipalities, purpose, and those inflicting damage or destruction. Number 1, you see Mostar, and then the then-existing municipalities. There were six of them; north, Stari Grad, south-east, south, and so on. In the north municipality, one was destroyed. In Stari Grad, ten. In Jugo -- or south-east municipality, 12. And then the next column denotes what was destroyed by Serb forces individually and collectively. A total of 30 were destroyed by Serbs. A total of 30 mosques. And 39 mesdzids were destroyed by Serbs. Then the next row denotes what was destroyed by Croats. Mesdzid is a mosque without a minaret. There were a total of three of them destroyed by the Croats. And a total of 50 mosques were destroyed by them. And then we have the next category, which has to do with destruction, or rather, with damage. That is to say that these facilities were destroyed -- damaged but not fully destroyed. 19 were damaged, 19 mosques and three mesdzids were damaged by Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I think we will have to, for that document, leave it at that. I'm sure that if the Judges or counsel have other questions about it, they will put them to you. I would like the witness to be shown at this time a map, copy of a map that has been used in the courtroom before. I mean the map -- this particular map, but a -- that could be provided to the witness, please, and if we could have a -- sorry. If we could have an In Court identification number for this, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can you please assign the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. This document will be assigned the reference number IC 00020. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And we have copies of this for the parties and for the Judges -- for Your Honours, I'm sorry. It should have been distributed before but here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, while this is being done - I think most people now have it - is what you have in front of you which has been marked for identification as IC 00020, a document, a map that has been provided to you since coming to The Hague and which you were asked to mark the locations of various destroyed or damaged mosques?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: This pertains to the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, in the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you look at that map, what's in front of you now, the hard copy that's on the ELMO, are the markings on that map markings that you made?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct. I personally marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And the markings that you have put on in numbers 1 through 8, do these correspond to the eight mosques destroyed in East Mostar as listed on pages 1 and 2 of your report?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: That's right. These are the mosques and areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And are the mosques that you have -- the locations that you have marked as 9, 10 and 11, are these locations damaged mosques in East Mostar that correspond to the three mosques listed on the second page of your report? At the top of the second page of your report?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, 9, 10 and what was the other number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Number 11 on your marking, and the --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the mosque number 3 in your report, the second page of your report, the Koski Mehmed-Pasina mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Number 11 is Koski Mehmed-pasa's mosque. You want me to check, right? It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And the markings that you have made on the map which are in your markings, A, B, C and D, do those correspond to the four mosques destroyed in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which are also listed -- sorry, in page 3 of your report?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC
utterances.text: These are the locations of the mosques destroyed in West Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I would conclude with that. By my records, for the record - and I certainly will be governed by the Registry's records - but I would just like to comment that according to our records, I have spent 3 hours and 43 minutes; considerably less time than the time I had forecast. There are other things I would go into but, because of the time limit, we will not be able to. Thank you. And thank you to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Scott, I take it that you have finished the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, to be precise, Your Honour, I think you told me that I was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to make sure, I don't want there to be a problem later on, saying that he was not allowed to finish his direct examination. He did indicate, "in the interests of time." I want to make sure that later on there is not some sort of an excuse that he wasn't allowed to present his case --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- because I'm certainly willing to give him all the time he wants. He can have all the time he wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We have an opportunity to start tomorrow at 8.30, that is to say half an hour earlier so that the witness can leave the Tribunal tomorrow, and doesn't need to stay here longer. Mr. Scott, you can be given another 15 minutes, in which case the Defence will have for their cross-examination until 1.45. But then you have to promise that you will spend no more than 15 minutes, not a second more. We have 40 seconds of tape remaining. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will -- I will use the 15 minutes and I just would like to cover some other documents very, very quickly and I will use the 15 minutes and be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We start tomorrow at 8.30. 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of May, 2006, at 8.30 a.m. 24 25
